blindSummary: Regional record: a rural, traditional state/province. The only state/province in the country found to have twice banned a Pride march from its capital's centre with the ban upheld - on 12 June 2025 the administration prohibited the 2025 Pride march in the state/province capital citing "risk of trouble to public order", the second consecutive year of the same restriction; the organisers' withdrawal citing LGBT visibility was itself called significant by the city. On 14 June 2025 the administrative court rejected the legal challenge, and the march (about 1,500 people per police) proceeded on a diverted route around the historic centre; the administration justified the ban by estimated organiser numbers (200 vs previous 2,500 and 1,500 turnouts) and a stated risk of violent individuals attaching themselves. The march itself passed peacefully ("joyful and festive, without a hitch"); the documented concern is the restriction and its chilling effect on visibility, rather than any violence.
blindSourceSummaries: A news feature (Jan 2018): trans women incarcerated in the country on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal grey area and are punished beyond their alleged crimes - placement problems in the prison system. National prison-system context (not state/province-specific).

The national detention ombuds's opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty: based on about 40 referrals since 2010, finds serious violations of fundamental rights persist across all places of detention; recommendations also apply to intersex and non-binary persons. National prison-system context.

An international anti-torture organisation's blog: interview with the national detention ombuds about its 2021 opinion - trans persons deprived of liberty face constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; a new opinion was needed because the 2010 opinion had not resolved the problems. National prison-system context.
blindTangential: The 2025 Pride-march bans were motivated by broad public-order reasoning against an LGB-allies-and-trans community march rather than any trans-specific measure; their chilling effect reaches gender-nonconforming visibility in public spaces broadly, which is how a trans visitor may encounter them.
